title: The Fresh Start Effect

scenes.text: Why does your diet always start on a *Monday*?
scenes.vo: Why does your diet always start on a Monday?

scenes.text: Researchers tracked gym visits & searches for “diet”
scenes.vo: Researchers at Wharton tracked gym visits and Google searches for the word diet.

scenes.text: Spikes after: *New Year*, new weeks, new months, *birthdays*
scenes.vo: Both spiked after New Year, at the start of each week and month, and after birthdays.
This is the fresh start effect. Dates like these feel like a clean slate.

scenes.text:
They separate the *old you*
from the *new you*
scenes.vo: They draw a line between the old you, who made the mistakes, and the new you, who won't.

scenes.text: But you don't need to wait for Monday
scenes.vo: But you don't have to wait for Monday or January.

scenes.text: Make today the landmark: call it *Day 1*.
scenes.vo: Make today the landmark. Name it. Call it day one, and start.

scenes.text:
Follow *@inquisitive_bytes*
for a daily byte of behaviour science
scenes.vo: Follow Inquisitive Bytes for a daily byte of behaviour science.

caption:
Mondays, birthdays and 1st January feel like a clean slate. 🗓️ That's the fresh start effect. But you can create your own landmark anytime.

Comment 'DAY 1' if you're starting something today 👇
source: Dai, H., Milkman, K. L. & Riis, J. (2014). The Fresh Start Effect: Temporal Landmarks Motivate Aspirational Behavior. Management Science, 60(10).
